text: Maryam woke up and stretched. The sun was shining, so she smiled a big, sunny smile.
say: Maryam woke up and stretched. The sun was shining, so she smiled a big, sunny smile.

text: At breakfast she smiled at Mama. Mama smiled back. “Assalamu alaykum, my little sunshine!”
say: At breakfast she smiled at Mama. Mama smiled back. “Assalaamu alaikum, my little sunshine!”

text: On the way to the bus, Mama smiled at Aunty Salma, their neighbour. Aunty Salma smiled too.
say: On the way to the bus, Mama smiled at Aunty Salma, their neighbour. Aunty Salma smiled too.

text: Uncle Sami, the bus driver, looked tired today. Can you help Maryam?
say: Uncle Sami, the bus driver, looked tired today. Can you help Maryam?

text: Maryam smiled and waved. Uncle Sami smiled a big smile back!
say: Maryam smiled and waved. Uncle Sami smiled a big smile back!

text: At school, Zara sat all alone. Maryam sat next to her and smiled. Soon Zara was smiling too.
say: At school, Zara sat all alone. Maryam sat next to her and smiled. Soon Zara was smiling too.

text: That evening Baba asked, “Why is everyone so happy today?” Mama laughed. “It all started with one little smile!”
say: That evening Baba asked, “Why is everyone so happy today?” Mama laughed. “It all started with one little smile!”

text: What did Maryam give to everyone she met? A smile? A sweet? A balloon?
say: What did Maryam give to everyone she met? A smile? A sweet? A balloon?

text: A smile is a gift anyone can give, and it is a charity.
say: A smile is a gift anyone can give, and it is a charity.

text: Your smile in the face of your brother is a charity (sadaqah) for you.
say: Your smile in the face of your brother is a charity (sadaqah) for you.

text: It was dinner time. Mama made rice, and Teta brought her yummy dates.
say: It was dinner time. Mama made rice, and Tayta brought her yummy dates.

text: Little Adam was so hungry! He grabbed the food with his left hand, from Yusuf’s plate.
say: Little Adam was so hungry! He grabbed the food with his left hand, from Yusuf’s plate.

text: “Wait, Adam!” said Yusuf kindly. “First we say Bismillah. Then we eat with our right hand, from the food in front of us.”
say: “Wait, Adam!” said Yusuf kindly. “First we say Bismillaah. Then we eat with our right hand, from the food in front of us.”

text: Adam lifted his right hand high. Can you help him?
say: Adam lifted his right hand high. Can you help him?

text: “Bismillah!” said Adam, as loud as he could.
say: “Bismillaah!” said Adam, as loud as he could.

text: Everyone clapped. Adam ate from his own plate with his right hand. He did not spill one grain of rice!
say: Everyone clapped. Adam ate from his own plate with his right hand. He did not spill one grain of rice!

text: When dinner was finished, Jiddo smiled and said, “Alhamdulillah!” And Adam said it too.
say: When dinner was finished, Jiddoh smiled and said, “Alhamdu lillaah!” And Adam said it too.

text: What do we say before we eat? Goodbye? Bismillah? Hooray?
say: What do we say before we eat? Goodbye? Bismillaah? Hooray?

text: We say Bismillah, eat with our right hand, and eat from what is in front of us.
say: We say Bismillaah, eat with our right hand, and eat from what is in front of us.

text: Young boy, say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.
say: Young boy, say Bismillaah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you.

text: It was a very hot day. Yusuf and Bilal were playing ball in the garden.
say: It was a very hot day. Yusuf and Bilal were playing ball in the garden.

text: “Meow…” said a tiny, tired voice. Under the tree sat Misk, the cat, panting in the heat.
say: “Meow…” said a tiny, tired voice. Under the tree sat Missk, the cat, panting in the heat.

text: “Poor Misk is thirsty,” said Yusuf. He ran inside and filled a bowl with cool water.
say: “Poor Missk is thirsty,” said Yusuf. He ran inside and filled a bowl with cool water.

text: Now Misk needs her water. Where should the bowl go?
say: Now Missk needs her water. Where should the bowl go?

text: Lap, lap, lap! Misk drank and drank.
say: Lap, lap, lap! Missk drank and drank.

text: Misk purred and rubbed against Yusuf’s legs. “I think she is saying thank you!” laughed Bilal.
say: Missk purred and rubbed against Yusuf’s legs. “I think she is saying thank you!” laughed Bilal.

text: Mama smiled from the window. “Allah loves it when we are kind to every living thing, big or small.”
say: Mama smiled from the window. “Allah loves it when we are kind to every living thing, big or small.”

text: How did Yusuf help Misk? He chased her away? He gave her water? He forgot about her?
say: How did Yusuf help Missk? He chased her away? He gave her water? He forgot about her?

text: Being kind to animals is a good deed that Allah rewards.
say: Being kind to animals is a good deed that Allah rewards.

text: There is a reward for kindness to every living creature.
say: There is a reward for kindness to every living creature.

text: Yusuf had a new red ball. “Just one little bounce inside,” he thought. Bounce… bounce…
say: Yusuf had a new red ball. “Just one little bounce inside,” he thought. Bounce… bounce…

text: CRASH! The ball hit Mama’s blue vase. It fell down and broke into pieces.
say: CRASH! The ball hit Mama’s blue vase. It fell down and broke into pieces.

text: Yusuf’s tummy felt funny. “Maybe I can hide the pieces,” he thought. “Or say Misk did it…”
say: Yusuf’s tummy felt funny. “Maybe I can hide the pieces,” he thought. “Or say Missk did it…”

text: But Yusuf knew that Allah sees everything, and that the truth is always best. What should he do?
say: But Yusuf knew that Allah sees everything, and that the truth is always best. What should he do?

text: “Mama, I am sorry. I bounced my ball inside, and I broke your vase.”
say: “Mama, I am sorry. I bounced my ball inside, and I broke your vase.”

text: Mama gave Yusuf a big hug. “Thank you for telling me the truth. That makes my heart happy.”
say: Mama gave Yusuf a big hug. “Thank you for telling me the truth. That makes my heart happy.”

text: They cleaned up together. “Balls are for outside,” said Mama. Yusuf nodded. “In sha Allah, I will remember!”
say: They cleaned up together. “Balls are for outside,” said Mama. Yusuf nodded. “In shaa Allah, I will remember!”

text: What brave thing did Yusuf do? He hid the pieces? He said Misk did it? He told the truth?
say: What brave thing did Yusuf do? He hid the pieces? He said Missk did it? He told the truth?

text: Telling the truth is brave, and it leads to goodness.
say: Telling the truth is brave, and it leads to goodness.

text: Truthfulness leads to goodness.
say: Truthfulness leads to goodness.

text: At weekend school, Ustadha Huda said, “Saying salam spreads love between people. Let’s say it to everyone this week!”
say: At weekend school, Ustaadha Huda said, “Saying salaam spreads love between people. Let’s say it to everyone this week!”

text: The next morning Yusuf said “Assalamu alaykum!” to Teta. “Wa alaykum assalam, my dear!” she said with a smile.
say: The next morning Yusuf said “Assalaamu alaikum!” to Tayta. “Wa alaikum assalaam, my dear!” she said with a smile.

text: He said salam to Aunty Salma, watering her flowers, and to Uncle Sami on the bus.
say: He said salaam to Aunty Salma, watering her flowers, and to Uncle Sami on the bus.

text: At school there was a new boy named Omar. He stood by the door, looking shy.
say: At school there was a new boy named Omar. He stood by the door, looking shy.

text: “Assalamu alaykum! I’m Yusuf.” Omar smiled. “Wa alaykum assalam! I’m Omar.”
say: “Assalaamu alaikum! I’m Yusuf.” Omar smiled. “Wa alaikum assalaam! I’m Omar.”

text: Yusuf showed Omar where to hang his coat. At lunch they sat together and shared their dates.
say: Yusuf showed Omar where to hang his coat. At lunch they sat together and shared their dates.

text: By the end of the week, Omar was Yusuf’s good friend. And it all began with one salam!
say: By the end of the week, Omar was Yusuf’s good friend. And it all began with one salaam!

text: What do we answer when someone says “Assalamu alaykum”? Wa alaykum assalam? Goodnight? Thank you?
say: What do we answer when someone says “Assalaamu alaikum”? Wa alaikum assalaam? Goodnight? Thank you?

text: We answer the salam with “Wa alaykum assalam”, or with something even better.
say: We answer the salaam with “Wa alaikum assalaam”, or with something even better.

text: Spread salam among yourselves (and you will love one another).
say: Spread salaam among yourselves (and you will love one another).

text: Teta baked her famous date cookies. Mmm! The whole house smelled warm and sweet.
say: Tayta baked her famous date cookies. Mmm! The whole house smelled warm and sweet.

text: Everyone had some. Soon there were only two cookies left on the plate, and Maryam took them both.
say: Everyone had some. Soon there were only two cookies left on the plate, and Maryam took them both.

text: Then she saw little Adam. He had dropped his cookie, and now he was crying.
say: Then she saw little Adam. He had dropped his cookie, and now he was crying.

text: Maryam thought, “If I were Adam, I would want a cookie too.” What will she do?
say: Maryam thought, “If I were Adam, I would want a cookie too.” What will she do?

text: “Here, Adam. One for you, and one for me!”
say: “Here, Adam. One for you, and one for me!”

text: Adam stopped crying and gave Maryam a big, crumbly hug.
say: Adam stopped crying and gave Maryam a big, crumbly hug.

text: Maryam’s one cookie tasted even sweeter than two. Teta said, “Masha’Allah! You loved for your brother what you love for yourself.”
say: Maryam’s one cookie tasted even sweeter than two. Tayta said, “Maashaa Allah! You loved for your brother what you love for yourself.”

text: Why did Maryam share her cookie? She did not like cookies? She wanted Adam to be happy, like her? Teta told her to?
say: Why did Maryam share her cookie? She did not like cookies? She wanted Adam to be happy, like her? Tayta told her to?

text: A believer loves for others what he loves for himself.
say: A believer loves for others what he loves for himself.

text: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.
say: None of you truly believes until he loves for his brother what he loves for himself.

text: Every Friday, Yusuf walks to the masjid with Jiddo. Jiddo walks slowly, with his wooden stick.
say: Every Friday, Yusuf walks to the masjid with Jiddoh. Jiddoh walks slowly, with his wooden stick.

text: Halfway there, Jiddo’s stick knocked against a big stone in the middle of the path. He nearly tripped!
say: Halfway there, Jiddoh’s stick knocked against a big stone in the middle of the path. He nearly tripped!

text: “Someone else might fall over it,” said Yusuf. “A little child, or someone who cannot see well.”
say: “Someone else might fall over it,” said Yusuf. “A little child, or someone who cannot see well.”

text: Let’s help Yusuf make the path safe.
say: Let’s help Yusuf make the path safe.

text: Heave-ho! Yusuf rolled the big stone to the side of the path.
say: Heave-ho! Yusuf rolled the big stone to the side of the path.

text: Jiddo’s eyes twinkled. “Masha’Allah, Yusuf! Moving something harmful out of the way is a charity.”
say: Jiddoh’s eyes twinkled. “Maashaa Allah, Yusuf! Moving something harmful out of the way is a charity.”

text: On the way home, Yusuf picked up a banana peel and a sharp can, and put them in the bin. The path was safe for everyone!
say: On the way home, Yusuf picked up a banana peel and a sharp can, and put them in the bin. The path was safe for everyone!

text: Why did Yusuf move the stone? So that nobody would trip? To keep it as a toy? To throw it?
say: Why did Yusuf move the stone? So that nobody would trip? To keep it as a toy? To throw it?

text: Making the way safe for others is a charity.
say: Making the way safe for others is a charity.

text: Removing something harmful from the road is a charity.
say: Removing something harmful from the road is a charity.

text: Every morning, Uncle Sami drives Bilal to school in the big yellow bus. Bilal jumps on and runs to his seat.
say: Every morning, Uncle Sami drives Bilal to school in the big yellow bus. Bilal jumps on and runs to his seat.

text: One rainy day, Bilal forgot his umbrella. Uncle Sami held his own big umbrella over Bilal, all the way to the school door.
say: One rainy day, Bilal forgot his umbrella. Uncle Sami held his own big umbrella over Bilal, all the way to the school door.

text: Bilal stopped. Uncle Sami was wet, but Bilal was dry. What should Bilal say?
say: Bilal stopped. Uncle Sami was wet, but Bilal was dry. What should Bilal say?

text: “Jazakallahu khayran, Uncle Sami!” Uncle Sami smiled from ear to ear.
say: “Jazaakallaahu khairan, Uncle Sami!” Uncle Sami smiled from ear to ear.

text: “It means: may Allah reward you with goodness,” Bilal told his friends. Saying thank you made two people happy!
say: “It means: may Allah reward you with goodness,” Bilal told his friends. Saying thank you made two people happy!

text: That evening Bilal thanked Mama for his lunch, and Baba for fixing his bike. Their faces lit up.
say: That evening Bilal thanked Mama for his lunch, and Baba for fixing his bike. Their faces lit up.

text: At bedtime, Bilal raised his hands. “Alhamdulillah, thank You, Allah, for kind people and for everything You give me.”
say: At bedtime, Bilal raised his hands. “Alhamdu lillaah, thank You, Allah, for kind people and for everything You give me.”

text: What can we say to thank someone? Jazakallahu khayran? Go away? Nothing?
say: What can we say to thank someone? Jazaakallaahu khairan? Go away? Nothing?

text: Thanking people is part of thanking Allah.
say: Thanking people is part of thanking Allah.

text: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.
say: Whoever does not thank people does not thank Allah.

text: Yusuf built the tallest tower of blocks ever. It was almost as tall as he was!
say: Yusuf built the tallest tower of blocks ever. It was almost as tall as he was!

text: Then little Adam came crawling… and BUMP! The tower fell down.
say: Then little Adam came crawling… and BUMP! The tower fell down.

text: Yusuf felt hot inside, like a bubbling volcano. He wanted to shout and stamp his feet!
say: Yusuf felt hot inside, like a bubbling volcano. He wanted to shout and stamp his feet!

text: Baba came and knelt down. “When you feel angry, say A‘udhu billahi minash-shaytanir-rajim. If you are standing, sit down. And drink some water.”
say: Baba came and knelt down. “When you feel angry, say Aoodhu billaahi minash shaitaanir rajeem. If you are standing, sit down. And drink some water.”

text: Yusuf tried it. Can you help him calm down?
say: Yusuf tried it. Can you help him calm down?

text: Breathe in… breathe out… “A‘udhu billah.” The volcano went quiet.
say: Breathe in… breathe out… “Aoodhu billaah.” The volcano went quiet.

text: “Let’s build it again, together,” said Yusuf. Adam handed him the blocks, one by one. The new tower was even taller!
say: “Let’s build it again, together,” said Yusuf. Adam handed him the blocks, one by one. The new tower was even taller!

text: What can we do when we feel angry? Shout and hit? Say A‘udhu billah, sit down and drink water? Break things?
say: What can we do when we feel angry? Shout and hit? Say Aoodhu billaah, sit down and drink water? Break things?

text: A strong person is one who stays in control when angry.
say: A strong person is one who stays in control when angry.

text: The strong person is not the one who wins a wrestle. The strong one is the one who controls himself when he is angry.
say: The strong person is not the one who wins a wrestle. The strong one is the one who controls himself when he is angry.

text: “Race you to the park!” shouted Bilal. The children ran ahead, laughing.
say: “Race you to the park!” shouted Bilal. The children ran ahead, laughing.

text: But Zara looked back. Jiddo was walking very slowly with his stick, all alone, carrying a heavy bag.
say: But Zara looked back. Jiddoh was walking very slowly with his stick, all alone, carrying a heavy bag.

text: Zara wanted to run and play. But she also wanted to help Jiddo. What should she do?
say: Zara wanted to run and play. But she also wanted to help Jiddoh. What should she do?

text: “Can I carry your bag, Jiddo? Let’s walk together.”
say: “Can I carry your bag, Jiddoh? Let’s walk together.”

text: Yusuf and Bilal saw Zara and came running back. They walked with Jiddo, step by slow step.
say: Yusuf and Bilal saw Zara and came running back. They walked with Jiddoh, step by slow step.

text: At the park, Jiddo sat under a big tree and told them a story from when he was a little boy.
say: At the park, Jiddoh sat under a big tree and told them a story from when he was a little boy.

text: Then Jiddo raised his hands. “May Allah bless you, my kind children.” Their hearts felt as big as the sky.
say: Then Jiddoh raised his hands. “May Allah bless you, my kind children.” Their hearts felt as big as the sky.

text: How did the children show respect to Jiddo? They left him behind? They carried his bag and walked with him? They laughed at his slow steps?
say: How did the children show respect to Jiddoh? They left him behind? They carried his bag and walked with him? They laughed at his slow steps?

text: We are kind to the young and respectful to the old.
say: We are kind to the young and respectful to the old.

text: He is not one of us who is not merciful to our young ones and respectful to our elders.
say: He is not one of us who is not merciful to our young ones and respectful to our elders.

text: Mama was busy all day. She cooked, she cleaned, and she looked after baby Adam.
say: Mama was busy all day. She cooked, she cleaned, and she looked after baby Adam.

text: In the evening, Mama sat down and sighed. “I am so tired,” she said softly.
say: In the evening, Mama sat down and sighed. “I am so tired,” she said softly.

text: Yusuf and Maryam whispered together. “Let’s help Mama!” What can they do?
say: Yusuf and Maryam whispered together. “Let’s help Mama!” What can they do?

text: Yusuf set the table. Maryam folded the towels. Then they played with Adam so Mama could rest.
say: Yusuf set the table. Maryam folded the towels. Then they played with Adam so Mama could rest.

text: Maryam drew a card with flowers and a big heart. It said: “We love you, Mama!”
say: Maryam drew a card with flowers and a big heart. It said: “We love you, Mama!”

text: Mama hugged them both. “Masha’Allah! Where did these little helpers come from?”
say: Mama hugged them both. “Maashaa Allah! Where did these little helpers come from?”

text: That night Mama made a special dua for them. And Yusuf and Maryam made a dua for Mama too.
say: That night Mama made a special dua for them. And Yusuf and Maryam made a dua for Mama too.

text: Who deserves our kindness and help the most? Our mother? Our toys? Nobody?
say: Who deserves our kindness and help the most? Our mother? Our toys? Nobody?

text: The Prophet ﷺ said “your mother” three times, then “your father”.
say: The Prophet , peace be upon him, said “your mother” three times, then “your father”.

text: A man asked who most deserves his good company. The Prophet ﷺ said: your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father.
say: A man asked who most deserves his good company. The Prophet , peace be upon him, said: your mother, then your mother, then your mother, then your father.

text: Every night, Yusuf brushed his teeth while the tap sang: glug, glug, glug. The water ran and ran.
say: Every night, Yusuf brushed his teeth while the tap sang: glug, glug, glug. The water ran and ran.

text: Teta peeked in. “Yusuf, where is all that water going?” “Down the drain!” Yusuf giggled.
say: Tayta peeked in. “Yusuf, where is all that water going?” “Down the drain!” Yusuf giggled.

text: “Water is a gift from Allah,” said Teta. “Some children walk a long way to get just one bucket. We must not waste it.”
say: “Water is a gift from Allah,” said Tayta. “Some children walk a long way to get just one bucket. We must not waste it.”

text: The tap is still singing. Can you help Yusuf?
say: The tap is still singing. Can you help Yusuf?

text: Squeak! Yusuf turned off the tap and used a little cup of water instead.
say: Squeak! Yusuf turned off the tap and used a little cup of water instead.

text: The next day, Yusuf and Maryam gave the water left in their cups to the thirsty flowers.
say: The next day, Yusuf and Maryam gave the water left in their cups to the thirsty flowers.

text: At dinner, Yusuf took a small helping first. “I can always ask for more,” he said. Nothing was wasted, alhamdulillah!
say: At dinner, Yusuf took a small helping first. “I can always ask for more,” he said. Nothing was wasted, Alhamdu lillaah!

text: How can we save water when we brush our teeth? Let the tap run? Turn off the tap and use a cup? Splash it everywhere?
say: How can we save water when we brush our teeth? Let the tap run? Turn off the tap and use a cup? Splash it everywhere?

text: Allah tells us to eat and drink, but not to waste.
say: Allah tells us to eat and drink, but not to waste.

text: Eat and drink, but do not waste.
say: Eat and drink, but do not waste.

text: Maryam and Adam made mud pies in the garden. Squish, squash! Their hands were brown and sticky.
say: Maryam and Adam made mud pies in the garden. Squish, squash! Their hands were brown and sticky.

text: “Lunch is ready!” called Mama. Adam ran inside and reached for the bread with his muddy hands.
say: “Lunch is ready!” called Mama. Adam ran inside and reached for the bread with his muddy hands.

text: “Stop!” laughed Maryam. “Muslims love to be clean. First we wash our hands with soap.”
say: “Stop!” laughed Maryam. “Muslims love to be clean. First we wash our hands with soap.”

text: Can you help them make lots of bubbles?
say: Can you help them make lots of bubbles?

text: Scrub the palms, the backs, between the fingers… Rinse! Sparkling clean!
say: Scrub the palms, the backs, between the fingers… Rinse! Sparkling clean!

text: Later, Maryam watched Baba make wudu for salah. Hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, ears and feet.
say: Later, Maryam watched Baba make wudoo for salaah. Hands, mouth, nose, face, arms, head, ears and feet.

text: Then they prayed together, fresh and clean. “Allah loves those who keep themselves clean,” said Baba.
say: Then they prayed together, fresh and clean. “Allah loves those who keep themselves clean,” said Baba.

text: What do we do before we eat? Wash our hands? Play in the mud? Wipe our hands on our clothes?
say: What do we do before we eat? Wash our hands? Play in the mud? Wipe our hands on our clothes?

text: Being clean is a big part of being a Muslim.
say: Being clean is a big part of being a Muslim.

text: Being clean is half of faith.
say: Being clean is half of faith.

text: A new neighbour moved in next door. Her name was Aunty Salma, and she lived all by herself.
say: A new neighbour moved in next door. Her name was Aunty Salma, and she lived all by herself.

text: From the window, Maryam saw her sitting on her step. “Mama, I think Aunty Salma is lonely.”
say: From the window, Maryam saw her sitting on her step. “Mama, I think Aunty Salma is lonely.”

text: “Let’s welcome her,” said Mama. Together they baked date cookies and put them in a pretty box.
say: “Let’s welcome her,” said Mama. Together they baked date cookies and put them in a pretty box.

text: They walked next door. Can you knock on the door with Maryam?
say: They walked next door. Can you knock on the door with Maryam?

text: “Assalamu alaykum, Aunty Salma! Welcome to our street!”
say: “Assalaamu alaikum, Aunty Salma! Welcome to our street!”

text: Aunty Salma’s eyes shone. She picked flowers from her garden for Maryam to take home.
say: Aunty Salma’s eyes shone. She picked flowers from her garden for Maryam to take home.

text: Now Aunty Salma comes for tea every Friday. “A good neighbour is a treasure,” she says.
say: Now Aunty Salma comes for tea every Friday. “A good neighbour is a treasure,” she says.

text: How did Maryam and Mama welcome their new neighbour? They ignored her? They brought her a gift and said salam? They made noise all night?
say: How did Maryam and Mama welcome their new neighbour? They ignored her? They brought her a gift and said salaam? They made noise all night?

text: Islam teaches us to be very good to our neighbours.
say: Islam teaches us to be very good to our neighbours.

text: Jibril kept telling me to be good to the neighbour, so much that I thought he would make the neighbour part of the family.
say: Jibril kept telling me to be good to the neighbour, so much that I thought he would make the neighbour part of the family.

text: At weekend school, Ustadha Huda gave each child a tiny seed. “Plant it, water it, and be patient,” she said.
say: At weekend school, Ustaadha Huda gave each child a tiny seed. “Plant it, water it, and be patient,” she said.

text: Maryam planted her seed in a pot by the window, and gave it a little drink of water.
say: Maryam planted her seed in a pot by the window, and gave it a little drink of water.

text: The next morning she ran to look. Nothing! Not even a tiny green leaf. “Hmph,” said Maryam.
say: The next morning she ran to look. Nothing! Not even a tiny green leaf. “Hmph,” said Maryam.

text: Teta said, “Good things take time. Keep caring for it, and make dua.” So every day, Maryam watered her seed and waited.
say: Tayta said, “Good things take time. Keep caring for it, and make dua.” So every day, Maryam watered her seed and waited.

text: One, two, three, four, five days… Look at the pot!
say: One, two, three, four, five days… Look at the pot!

text: A little green sprout! SubhanAllah!
say: A little green sprout! Subhaan Allah!

text: Weeks later, Maryam’s plant had a bright yellow flower. “Being patient was worth it!” she smiled.
say: Weeks later, Maryam’s plant had a bright yellow flower. “Being patient was worth it!” she smiled.

text: What did Maryam learn? To give up quickly? To be patient and keep trying? That seeds never grow?
say: What did Maryam learn? To give up quickly? To be patient and keep trying? That seeds never grow?

text: Allah is with those who are patient.
say: Allah is with those who are patient.

text: Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient.
say: Indeed, Allah is with those who are patient.

text: Bilal wanted to learn Surah al-Ikhlas all in one go. He read it again and again and again.
say: Bilal wanted to learn Surah al-Ikhlas all in one go. He read it again and again and again.

text: Soon his eyes felt heavy, and the words got all mixed up. “I can’t do it!” he said.
say: Soon his eyes felt heavy, and the words got all mixed up. “I can’t do it!” he said.

text: Jiddo pointed at a little bird by the window. “See how it drinks? A little sip, then another. Let’s learn one ayah each day.”
say: Jiddoh pointed at a little bird by the window. “See how it drinks? A little sip, then another. Let’s learn one ayah each day.”

text: Monday, one ayah. Tuesday, the next one. Wednesday, one more. Can you help Bilal finish on Thursday?
say: Monday, one ayah. Tuesday, the next one. Wednesday, one more. Can you help Bilal finish on Thursday?

text: Bilal knew all four ayahs! Masha’Allah!
say: Bilal knew all four ayahs! Maashaa Allah!

text: At weekend school, Bilal recited the whole surah to Ustadha Huda, without one mistake.
say: At weekend school, Bilal recited the whole surah to Ustaadha Huda, without one mistake.

text: “A little every day is the best way,” said Bilal. Now he learns a new ayah every morning, just like the little bird.
say: “A little every day is the best way,” said Bilal. Now he learns a new ayah every morning, just like the little bird.

text: What is the best way to learn? A little bit every day? Everything in one night? Never?
say: What is the best way to learn? A little bit every day? Everything in one night? Never?

text: The deeds Allah loves most are the ones we keep doing, even if they are small.
say: The deeds Allah loves most are the ones we keep doing, even if they are small.

text: The deeds most loved by Allah are those done regularly, even if they are small.
say: The deeds most loved by Allah are those done regularly, even if they are small.

text: Zara drew a picture of a garden with a big yellow sun. She was very proud of it.
say: Zara drew a picture of a garden with a big yellow sun. She was very proud of it.

text: Omar looked at it and said, “That’s a funny sun. It looks like a pancake!”
say: Omar looked at it and said, “That’s a funny sun. It looks like a pancake!”

text: Zara’s smile went away. Unkind words can hurt, even when they are said as a joke.
say: Zara’s smile went away. Unkind words can hurt, even when they are said as a joke.

text: Yusuf came over. What kind thing could he say?
say: Yusuf came over. What kind thing could he say?

text: “I love your colours, Zara! Your sun makes me feel warm.”
say: “I love your colours, Zara! Your sun makes me feel warm.”

text: Omar felt sorry. “Zara, I’m sorry. Can you show me how you drew those flowers?”
say: Omar felt sorry. “Zara, I’m sorry. Can you show me how you drew those flowers?”

text: Soon all three were drawing together. Kind words are like flowers: they make everyone’s day brighter.
say: Soon all three were drawing together. Kind words are like flowers: they make everyone’s day brighter.

text: What made Zara smile again? A kind word? A loud noise? Being left alone?
say: What made Zara smile again? A kind word? A loud noise? Being left alone?

text: A good word is a charity.
say: A good word is a charity.

text: Yusuf was saving coins in a jar. Clink, clink! He wanted to buy a shiny toy car.
say: Yusuf was saving coins in a jar. Clink, clink! He wanted to buy a shiny toy car.

text: At the masjid, the imam spoke about children far away who did not have enough food to eat.
say: At the masjid, the imam spoke about children far away who did not have enough food to eat.

text: Yusuf thought about his jar of coins. He thought about the hungry children. He thought very hard.
say: Yusuf thought about his jar of coins. He thought about the hungry children. He thought very hard.

text: The next Friday, Yusuf took his jar to the masjid. Can you help him?
say: The next Friday, Yusuf took his jar to the masjid. Can you help him?

text: Clink, clink, clink! Yusuf gave his coins to help the hungry children.
say: Clink, clink, clink! Yusuf gave his coins to help the hungry children.

text: Baba put his hand on Yusuf’s shoulder. “The hand that gives is better than the hand that takes. I am proud of you.”
say: Baba put his hand on Yusuf’s shoulder. “The hand that gives is better than the hand that takes. I am proud of you.”

text: Yusuf did not get the toy car that week. But his heart felt warm and full, and he knew Allah saw his good deed.
say: Yusuf did not get the toy car that week. But his heart felt warm and full, and he knew Allah saw his good deed.

text: Which hand is better, the one that gives or the one that takes? The hand that gives? The hand that takes? Neither?
say: Which hand is better, the one that gives or the one that takes? The hand that gives? The hand that takes? Neither?

text: Giving to others is loved by Allah.
say: Giving to others is loved by Allah.

text: The upper hand (the one that gives) is better than the lower hand (the one that takes).
say: The upper hand (the one that gives) is better than the lower hand (the one that takes).

text: It was bedtime, but Adam was bouncing like a ball. “I’m not sleepy!” he said.
say: It was bedtime, but Adam was bouncing like a ball. “I’m not sleepy!” he said.

text: “Let me show you our bedtime way,” said Maryam. “First, we make wudu and brush our teeth.”
say: “Let me show you our bedtime way,” said Maryam. “First, we make wudoo and brush our teeth.”

text: “Then we lie down on our right side, and Mama reads the three Quls with us.”
say: “Then we lie down on our right side, and Mama reads the three Kulls with us.”

text: Now it is time for the sleeping dua. Can you say it with Adam?
say: Now it is time for the sleeping dua. Can you say it with Adam?

text: “Bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya.” In Your name, O Allah, I sleep and I wake.
say: “Bismika Allaahumma amootu wa ahyaa.” In Your name, O Allah, I sleep and I wake.

text: Adam yawned a great big yawn. His eyes closed slowly… slowly…
say: Adam yawned a great big yawn. His eyes closed slowly… slowly…

text: Even Misk curled up at the end of the bed. Goodnight, Adam. Goodnight, Misk. Goodnight, moon.
say: Even Missk curled up at the end of the bed. Goodnight, Adam. Goodnight, Missk. Goodnight, moon.

text: What do we do before we sleep? Jump on the bed all night? Make wudu, read the Quls and say our dua? Watch TV?
say: What do we do before we sleep? Jump on the bed all night? Make wudoo, read the Kulls and say our dua? Watch TV?

text: The Prophet ﷺ said a dua every night before he slept.
say: The Prophet , peace be upon him, said a dua every night before he slept.

text: When the Prophet ﷺ went to bed he said: “In Your name, O Allah, I die (sleep) and I live (wake).”
say: When the Prophet , peace be upon him, went to bed he said: “In Your name, O Allah, I die (sleep) and I live (wake).”

text: Yusuf put on his shoes for the park. But then… pitter, patter! It began to rain.
say: Yusuf put on his shoes for the park. But then… pitter, patter! It began to rain.

text: “Oh no! Now we can’t go out,” Yusuf grumbled, with his face pressed to the window.
say: “Oh no! Now we can’t go out,” Yusuf grumbled, with his face pressed to the window.

text: Teta sat beside him. “Look, Yusuf. The rain is a gift from Allah. Who is happy about the rain?”
say: Tayta sat beside him. “Look, Yusuf. The rain is a gift from Allah. Who is happy about the rain?”

text: Look outside! Tap the flowers and see who is happy.
say: Look outside! Tap the flowers and see who is happy.

text: The flowers drink, the trees drink, and the birds have water too. SubhanAllah!
say: The flowers drink, the trees drink, and the birds have water too. Subhaan Allah!

text: Teta taught him the dua for rain: “Allahumma sayyiban nafi‘a.” O Allah, make it a helpful rain.
say: Tayta taught him the dua for rain: “Allaahumma sayyiban naafiaa.” O Allah, make it a helpful rain.

text: When the rain stopped, Yusuf put on his boots and jumped in every puddle. “Alhamdulillah for the rain!” he laughed.
say: When the rain stopped, Yusuf put on his boots and jumped in every puddle. “Alhamdu lillaah for the rain!” he laughed.

text: What do we say for all of Allah’s gifts, even the rain? Alhamdulillah? Oh no? Nothing?
say: What do we say for all of Allah’s gifts, even the rain? Alhamdu lillaah? Oh no? Nothing?

text: When we are thankful, Allah gives us even more.
say: When we are thankful, Allah gives us even more.

text: If you are thankful, I will surely give you more.
say: If you are thankful, I will surely give you more.

text: It was Omar’s first day at weekend school. He did not know where anything was.
say: It was Omar’s first day at weekend school. He did not know where anything was.

text: Oops! Omar tripped, and his books and pencils went flying everywhere.
say: Oops! Omar tripped, and his books and pencils went flying everywhere.

text: Some children giggled. But Bilal did not giggle. What will Bilal do?
say: Some children giggled. But Bilal did not giggle. What will Bilal do?

text: “Don’t worry, I’ll help you!” Bilal picked up every book and pencil.
say: “Don’t worry, I’ll help you!” Bilal picked up every book and pencil.

text: Bilal showed Omar the coat hooks, the shoe rack and the wudu room. “Stick with me!” he said.
say: Bilal showed Omar the coat hooks, the shoe rack and the wudoo room. “Stick with me!” he said.

text: In class, Bilal’s work was hard today. Ustadha Huda gave him extra time and helped him, and he finished it all.
say: In class, Bilal’s work was hard today. Ustaadha Huda gave him extra time and helped him, and he finished it all.

text: “You helped Omar today,” said Ustadha Huda, “and Allah helped you. Allah helps us when we help others.”
say: “You helped Omar today,” said Ustaadha Huda, “and Allah helped you. Allah helps us when we help others.”

text: What did Bilal do when Omar dropped his books? He laughed? He helped pick them up? He walked away?
say: What did Bilal do when Omar dropped his books? He laughed? He helped pick them up? He walked away?

text: Allah helps us as long as we are helping others.
say: Allah helps us as long as we are helping others.

text: Allah helps His servant as long as the servant is helping his brother.
say: Allah helps His servant as long as the servant is helping his brother.

text: It was Eid! Zara had new shoes that sparkled in the sun. “Look how shiny they are!” she said.
say: It was Eid! Zara had new shoes that sparkled in the sun. “Look how shiny they are!” she said.

text: Maryam looked down at her old brown shoes. They had a little scratch. She felt a bit sad.
say: Maryam looked down at her old brown shoes. They had a little scratch. She felt a bit sad.

text: At the masjid door, everyone took off their shoes. Shiny ones, old ones, big ones and tiny ones, all in a row.
say: At the masjid door, everyone took off their shoes. Shiny ones, old ones, big ones and tiny ones, all in a row.

text: After the Eid prayer, an old lady could not reach the plate of dates. What can Maryam do?
say: After the Eid prayer, an old lady could not reach the plate of dates. What can Maryam do?

text: Maryam brought her the dates and a cup of water. “Eid Mubarak!”
say: Maryam brought her the dates and a cup of water. “Eed Mubaarak!”

text: Zara saw it all. “Maryam,” she said, “you didn’t need shiny shoes. You have the shiniest heart!”
say: Zara saw it all. “Maryam,” she said, “you didn’t need shiny shoes. You have the shiniest heart!”

text: Teta hugged Maryam. “Allah does not look at our shoes or our clothes. He looks at our hearts and what we do.”
say: Tayta hugged Maryam. “Allah does not look at our shoes or our clothes. He looks at our hearts and what we do.”

text: What does Allah look at? Our new shoes? Our hearts and our deeds? Our toys?
say: What does Allah look at? Our new shoes? Our hearts and our deeds? Our toys?

text: A kind heart and good deeds are what really shine.
say: A kind heart and good deeds are what really shine.

text: Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.
say: Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth, but He looks at your hearts and your deeds.

text: Masha’Allah, that’s right!
say: Maashaa Allah, that’s right!

text: Yes!
say: Yes!

text: Not quite. Try again!
say: Not quite. Try again!

text: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said:
say: The Prophet Muhammad , peace be upon him, said:

text: Allah says in the Qurʾan:
say: Allah says in the Quran:

text: The renewed digging of Zamzam by ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. Its traces had been worn away after the tribe of Jurhum filled it in, and so it remained until his time.
say: The renewed digging of Zamzam by Abdul Muttalib ibn Hashim. Its traces had been worn away after the tribe of Jurhum filled it in, and so it remained until his time.

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “I was sleeping in al-Hijr when someone came to me and said, ‘Dig Tayba.’ I said, ‘What is Tayba?’ Then he left me. The next day I went back to my bed and slept, and he came to me and said, ‘Dig Barra.’ I said, ‘What is Barra?’ Then he left me. The next day I went back to my bed and slept, and he came to me and said, ‘Dig al-Madnuna.’ I said, ‘What is al-Madnuna?’ Then he left me. The next day I went back to my bed and slept in it, and he came to me and said, ‘Dig Zamzam.’ I said, ‘What is Zamzam?’ He said, ‘It never runs dry and never fails. It gives water to the great gathering of pilgrims. It is between the dung and the blood, at the pecking place of the crow with the white mark, at the colony of the ants.’”
say: Abdul Muttalib said: “I was sleeping in al-Hijr when someone came to me and said, ‘Dig Tayba.’ I said, ‘What is Tayba?’ Then he left me. The next day I went back to my bed and slept, and he came to me and said, ‘Dig Barra.’ I said, ‘What is Barra?’ Then he left me. The next day I went back to my bed and slept, and he came to me and said, ‘Dig al-Madnuna.’ I said, ‘What is al-Madnuna?’ Then he left me. The next day I went back to my bed and slept in it, and he came to me and said, ‘Dig Zamzam.’ I said, ‘What is Zamzam?’ He said, ‘It never runs dry and never fails. It gives water to the great gathering of pilgrims. It is between the dung and the blood, at the pecking place of the crow with the white mark, at the colony of the ants.’”

text: When its matter had been made clear to him and its place had been shown to him, and he knew he had been told the truth, he set out in the morning with his pickaxe, and with him his son al-Harith ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, who was his only son at that time. He dug, and when the stone lining of the old well appeared, ʿAbd al-Muttalib called out “Allahu akbar”, and Quraysh knew that he had found what he was looking for.
say: When its matter had been made clear to him and its place had been shown to him, and he knew he had been told the truth, he set out in the morning with his pickaxe, and with him his son al-Harith ibn Abdul Muttalib, who was his only son at that time. He dug, and when the stone lining of the old well appeared, Abdul Muttalib called out “Allahu akbar”, and Quraysh knew that he had found what he was looking for.

text: They came to him and said: “ʿAbd al-Muttalib, this is the well of our father Ismaʿil, and we have a right to it. Give us a share in it with you.” He said: “I will not. This matter was given to me alone, out of all of you.” They said: “Then be fair to us, for we will not leave you until we have taken you to judgement over it.”
say: They came to him and said: “Abdul Muttalib, this is the well of our father Ismail, and we have a right to it. Give us a share in it with you.” He said: “I will not. This matter was given to me alone, out of all of you.” They said: “Then be fair to us, for we will not leave you until we have taken you to judgement over it.”

text: He said: “Choose whomever you wish to judge between us.” They said: “The soothsayer of Banu Saʿd ibn Hudhaym.” He agreed. She lived in the highlands of al-Sham. ʿAbd al-Muttalib rode out with a group of his family, and a group rode from every clan of Quraysh. In those days the land between was open desert. When they were part of the way, ʿAbd al-Muttalib and his companions ran out of water. They grew so thirsty that they were sure they would die. They asked the others for water, but they refused, saying: “We are in the desert, and we fear for ourselves what has happened to you.”
say: He said: “Choose whomever you wish to judge between us.” They said: “The soothsayer of Banu Sad ibn Hudhaym.” He agreed. She lived in the highlands of al-Sham. Abdul Muttalib rode out with a group of his family, and a group rode from every clan of Quraysh. In those days the land between was open desert. When they were part of the way, Abdul Muttalib and his companions ran out of water. They grew so thirsty that they were sure they would die. They asked the others for water, but they refused, saying: “We are in the desert, and we fear for ourselves what has happened to you.”

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “I think each of you should dig his own grave while you still have the strength, so that whenever one dies his companions can bury him, until only one man is left. The loss of one man is easier than the loss of a whole caravan.” They said: “What you advise is good.” Each man dug a grave for himself, and they sat waiting for death, thirsty.
say: Abdul Muttalib said: “I think each of you should dig his own grave while you still have the strength, so that whenever one dies his companions can bury him, until only one man is left. The loss of one man is easier than the loss of a whole caravan.” They said: “What you advise is good.” Each man dug a grave for himself, and they sat waiting for death, thirsty.

text: Then ʿAbd al-Muttalib said to his companions: “Have we thrown ourselves into the hands of death like this, without travelling on and seeking for ourselves, out of weakness? Perhaps Allah will provide us with water somewhere in the land.” So they set off. When ʿAbd al-Muttalib made his camel rise, a spring of sweet water burst out from under its hoof. ʿAbd al-Muttalib said “Allahu akbar”, and his companions said it too. He dismounted and drank, and his companions drank, and they filled their water-skins. Then he called the clans of Quraysh, who had been watching all of this: “Come to the water, for Allah has given us water.” They came and drank and filled their water-skins.
say: Then Abdul Muttalib said to his companions: “Have we thrown ourselves into the hands of death like this, without travelling on and seeking for ourselves, out of weakness? Perhaps Allah will provide us with water somewhere in the land.” So they set off. When Abdul Muttalib made his camel rise, a spring of sweet water burst out from under its hoof. Abdul Muttalib said “Allahu akbar”, and his companions said it too. He dismounted and drank, and his companions drank, and they filled their water-skins. Then he called the clans of Quraysh, who had been watching all of this: “Come to the water, for Allah has given us water.” They came and drank and filled their water-skins.

text: All of them. Then they said: “By Allah, the judgement has been given for you against us. By Allah, we will never dispute with you over Zamzam. The One who gave you this water in this desert is the One who gave you Zamzam. Go back to your watering of the pilgrims, rightly guided.” He went back and they went back with him. They never reached the soothsayer, and they left him and Zamzam alone.
say: All of them. Then they said: “By Allah, the judgement has been given for you against us. By Allah, we will never dispute with you over Zamzam. The One who gave you this water in this desert is the One who gave you Zamzam. Go back to your watering of the pilgrims, rightly guided.” He went back and they went back with him. They never reached the soothsayer, and they left him and Zamzam alone.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: They claim that when this was said to him, ʿAbd al-Muttalib asked: “And where is it?” He was told: “At the colony of the ants, where the crow will peck tomorrow.” Allah knows best which of these it was.
say: Ibn Ishaq said: They claim that when this was said to him, Abdul Muttalib asked: “And where is it?” He was told: “At the colony of the ants, where the crow will peck tomorrow.” Allah knows best which of these it was.

text: Al-Umawi adds that ʿAbd al-Muttalib found the colony of the ants and the crow pecking beside it, between two idols of Quraysh. Quraysh objected to his digging there; he told his son al-Harith to keep them back, and when they saw he would not give up, they left him to dig. As he dug deeper he found two gazelles of gold that Jurhum had buried, with swords and coats of armour.
say: Al-Umawi adds that Abdul Muttalib found the colony of the ants and the crow pecking beside it, between two idols of Quraysh. Quraysh objected to his digging there; he told his son al-Harith to keep them back, and when they saw he would not give up, they left him to dig. As he dug deeper he found two gazelles of gold that Jurhum had buried, with swords and coats of armour.

text: Then ʿAbd al-Muttalib set up the watering of the pilgrims from Zamzam. Ibn Ishaq and others mention that there were many wells in Makkah before Zamzam appeared in the time of ʿAbd al-Muttalib … and Zamzam surpassed all the wells, and all the people turned to it, because of its place by the Sacred Mosque, its excellence over all other water, and because it is the well of Ismaʿil son of Ibrahim.
say: Then Abdul Muttalib set up the watering of the pilgrims from Zamzam. Ibn Ishaq and others mention that there were many wells in Makkah before Zamzam appeared in the time of Abdul Muttalib … and Zamzam surpassed all the wells, and all the people turned to it, because of its place by the Sacred Mosque, its excellence over all other water, and because it is the well of Ismail son of Ibrahim.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: Then Abraha built al-Qullays in Sanaʿa, a church whose like had not been seen anywhere on earth in its time, and he wrote to the Negus: “I have built for you a church like none ever built for a king before you, and I will not stop until I have turned the pilgrimage of the Arabs to it.”
say: Ibn Ishaq said: Then Abraha built al-Qullays in Sanaa, a church whose like had not been seen anywhere on earth in its time, and he wrote to the Negus: “I have built for you a church like none ever built for a king before you, and I will not stop until I have turned the pilgrimage of the Arabs to it.”

text: When the Arabs spoke of Abraha’s letter to the Negus, a man of Kinanah was angered. He went to al-Qullays and showed his contempt for it, then went back to his own land. Abraha was told that a man from the people of the House in Makkah had done this when he heard of Abraha’s plan to turn the pilgrimage away from it. Abraha was enraged, and swore that he would march on the House and destroy it.
say: When the Arabs spoke of Abraha’s letter to the Negus, a man of Kinanah was angered. He went to al-Qullays and showed his contempt for it, then went back to his own land. Abraha was told that a man from the people of the House in Makkah had done this when he heard of Abraha’s plan to turn the pilgrimage away from it. Abraha was enraged, and swore that he would march on the House and destroy it.

text: Then he ordered the Abyssinians to prepare, and they made ready. He set out, taking the elephant with him. The Arabs heard of it and were horrified, and they saw it as their duty to fight him when they heard that he meant to destroy the Kaʿbah, the Sacred House of Allah. A man of the nobles and kings of Yemen called Dhu Nafr called his people and other Arabs to fight Abraha and defend the Sacred House. He met him in battle, but Dhu Nafr and his men were defeated, and Dhu Nafr was taken captive.
say: Then he ordered the Abyssinians to prepare, and they made ready. He set out, taking the elephant with him. The Arabs heard of it and were horrified, and they saw it as their duty to fight him when they heard that he meant to destroy the Kabah, the Sacred House of Allah. A man of the nobles and kings of Yemen called Dhu Nafr called his people and other Arabs to fight Abraha and defend the Sacred House. He met him in battle, but Dhu Nafr and his men were defeated, and Dhu Nafr was taken captive.

text: When Abraha reached the land of Khathʿam, Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khathʿami came against him with the two tribes of Khathʿam and the Arabs who followed him. Abraha defeated him and took him captive. When he meant to kill him, Nufayl said: “O king, do not kill me, for I will be your guide in the land of the Arabs.” So Abraha let him go.
say: When Abraha reached the land of Khatham, Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khathami came against him with the two tribes of Khatham and the Arabs who followed him. Abraha defeated him and took him captive. When he meant to kill him, Nufayl said: “O king, do not kill me, for I will be your guide in the land of the Arabs.” So Abraha let him go.

text: He took him along as his guide. When he passed by al-Taʾif, Masʿud ibn Muʿattib came out to him with men of Thaqif and said: “O king, we will not oppose you. This house of ours is not the House you want. You want the House in Makkah, and we will send someone with you to guide you to it.” They sent Abu Righal with him to show him the way to Makkah. Abraha set out with Abu Righal until he brought him to al-Mughammas.
say: He took him along as his guide. When he passed by al-Taif, Masud ibn Muattib came out to him with men of Thaqif and said: “O king, we will not oppose you. This house of ours is not the House you want. You want the House in Makkah, and we will send someone with you to guide you to it.” They sent Abu Righal with him to show him the way to Makkah. Abraha set out with Abu Righal until he brought him to al-Mughammas.

text: When Abraha camped at al-Mughammas, he sent an Abyssinian called al-Aswad ibn Mafsud with horsemen to Makkah. He drove off to Abraha the wealth of the people of Tihama, from Quraysh and others, and among it were two hundred camels of ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, who was then the eldest and leader of Quraysh. Quraysh, Kinanah, Hudhayl and the others in the Haram thought of fighting him; then they knew they had no power to fight him, and they left it.
say: When Abraha camped at al-Mughammas, he sent an Abyssinian called al-Aswad ibn Mafsud with horsemen to Makkah. He drove off to Abraha the wealth of the people of Tihama, from Quraysh and others, and among it were two hundred camels of Abdul Muttalib ibn Hashim, who was then the eldest and leader of Quraysh. Quraysh, Kinanah, Hudhayl and the others in the Haram thought of fighting him; then they knew they had no power to fight him, and they left it.

text: Abraha sent Hunata al-Himyari to Makkah and told him: “Ask for the leader and noblest man of this land and tell him: The king says, I have not come to fight you. I have come only to destroy this House. If you do not stand against us to defend it, I have no need of your blood.” When Hunata entered Makkah he asked for the leader of Quraysh, and was told: ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim. He went to him and told him what Abraha had said. ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “By Allah, we do not want to fight him, and we have no power to do so. This is the Sacred House of Allah and the house of His Khalil Ibrahim, peace be upon him. If He protects it from him, it is His Sanctuary and His House; and if He leaves it to him, by Allah, we have no way to defend it.”
say: Abraha sent Hunata al-Himyari to Makkah and told him: “Ask for the leader and noblest man of this land and tell him: The king says, I have not come to fight you. I have come only to destroy this House. If you do not stand against us to defend it, I have no need of your blood.” When Hunata entered Makkah he asked for the leader of Quraysh, and was told: Abdul Muttalib ibn Hashim. He went to him and told him what Abraha had said. Abdul Muttalib said: “By Allah, we do not want to fight him, and we have no power to do so. This is the Sacred House of Allah and the house of His Khalil Ibrahim, peace be upon him. If He protects it from him, it is His Sanctuary and His House; and if He leaves it to him, by Allah, we have no way to defend it.”

text: Hunata said: “Then come with me to him, for he has ordered me to bring you.” ʿAbd al-Muttalib went with him, with some of his sons, until he reached the camp. He asked for Dhu Nafr, who was his friend, and went in to him in his prison. Dhu Nafr said: “What help can a captive be, who expects the king to kill him morning or evening? But Unays, the keeper of the elephant, is my friend. I will send for him, commend you to him, and ask him to get you leave to see the king.” Unays spoke to Abraha: “O king, the leader of Quraysh is at your door asking to see you. He is the master of the well of Makkah, who feeds people in the plain and the wild animals on the mountain tops.” Abraha gave him leave.
say: Hunata said: “Then come with me to him, for he has ordered me to bring you.” Abdul Muttalib went with him, with some of his sons, until he reached the camp. He asked for Dhu Nafr, who was his friend, and went in to him in his prison. Dhu Nafr said: “What help can a captive be, who expects the king to kill him morning or evening? But Unays, the keeper of the elephant, is my friend. I will send for him, commend you to him, and ask him to get you leave to see the king.” Unays spoke to Abraha: “O king, the leader of Quraysh is at your door asking to see you. He is the master of the well of Makkah, who feeds people in the plain and the wild animals on the mountain tops.” Abraha gave him leave.

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib was the most handsome and dignified of men. When Abraha saw him he honoured him, and he would not seat him below himself, nor let the Abyssinians see him seat him on his throne. So he came down from his throne and sat on his carpet, and seated ʿAbd al-Muttalib beside him. He said to his interpreter: “Ask him what he needs.” ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “My need is that the king return to me two hundred camels he has taken from me.” Abraha said to his interpreter: “Tell him: I admired you when I saw you, but I think less of you now that you have spoken. You speak to me about two hundred camels I took from you, and say nothing of a House that is your religion and the religion of your fathers, which I have come to destroy?” ʿAbd al-Muttalib said: “I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.” Abraha said: “He will not protect it from me.” He said: “That is between you and Him.” And Abraha returned his camels to him.
say: Abdul Muttalib was the most handsome and dignified of men. When Abraha saw him he honoured him, and he would not seat him below himself, nor let the Abyssinians see him seat him on his throne. So he came down from his throne and sat on his carpet, and seated Abdul Muttalib beside him. He said to his interpreter: “Ask him what he needs.” Abdul Muttalib said: “My need is that the king return to me two hundred camels he has taken from me.” Abraha said to his interpreter: “Tell him: I admired you when I saw you, but I think less of you now that you have spoken. You speak to me about two hundred camels I took from you, and say nothing of a House that is your religion and the religion of your fathers, which I have come to destroy?” Abdul Muttalib said: “I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.” Abraha said: “He will not protect it from me.” He said: “That is between you and Him.” And Abraha returned his camels to him.

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib went back to Quraysh, told them the news, and ordered them to leave Makkah and take refuge on the mountain tops, out of fear of the harm the army would do to them. Then ʿAbd al-Muttalib stood and took hold of the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah, and a group of Quraysh stood with him, calling on Allah and asking Him for help against Abraha and his army.
say: Abdul Muttalib went back to Quraysh, told them the news, and ordered them to leave Makkah and take refuge on the mountain tops, out of fear of the harm the army would do to them. Then Abdul Muttalib stood and took hold of the ring of the door of the Kabah, and a group of Quraysh stood with him, calling on Allah and asking Him for help against Abraha and his army.

text: And ʿAbd al-Muttalib said, holding the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah: “O Allah, a man protects his own dwelling, so protect Your dwelling. Let their cross and their might never overcome Your might tomorrow. And if You leave them and our qibla, then command what You will.” Ibn Hisham said: this is what is authentic of it.
say: And Abdul Muttalib said, holding the ring of the door of the Kabah: “O Allah, a man protects his own dwelling, so protect Your dwelling. Let their cross and their might never overcome Your might tomorrow. And if You leave them and our qibla, then command what You will.” Ibn Hisham said: this is what is authentic of it.

text: Then ʿAbd al-Muttalib let go of the ring of the door of the Kaʿbah, and he and the Quraysh with him went off to the mountain peaks to shelter there and wait to see what Abraha would do.
say: Then Abdul Muttalib let go of the ring of the door of the Kabah, and he and the Quraysh with him went off to the mountain peaks to shelter there and wait to see what Abraha would do.

text: In the morning Abraha prepared to enter Makkah. He made his elephant ready and drew up his army; the elephant’s name was Mahmud. When they turned the elephant towards Makkah, Nufayl ibn Habib came and stood beside it, took hold of its ear and said: “Kneel, Mahmud, and go back safely to where you came from, for you are in the Sacred Land of Allah.” And he let go of its ear. The elephant knelt. Nufayl ran off and climbed the mountain. They beat the elephant to make it stand, but it refused. They turned it back towards Yemen, and it got up and hurried off. They turned it towards al-Sham and it did the same, and towards the east and it did the same. They turned it towards Makkah, and it knelt.
say: In the morning Abraha prepared to enter Makkah. He made his elephant ready and drew up his army; the elephant’s name was Mahmud. When they turned the elephant towards Makkah, Nufayl ibn Habib came and stood beside it, took hold of its ear and said: “Kneel, Mahmud, and go back safely to where you came from, for you are in the Sacred Land of Allah.” And he let go of its ear. The elephant knelt. Nufayl ran off and climbed the mountain. They beat the elephant to make it stand, but it refused. They turned it back towards Yemen, and it got up and hurried off. They turned it towards al-Sham and it did the same, and towards the east and it did the same. They turned it towards Makkah, and it knelt.

text: And Allah sent upon them birds from the sea, like swallows, each bird carrying three stones: one in its beak and two in its feet, like chickpeas and lentils. No one they struck escaped, though not all of them were struck. They fled, rushing back along the road by which they had come.
say: And Allah sent upon them birds from the sea, like swallows, each bird carrying three stones: one in its beak and two in its feet, like chickpeas and lentils. No one they struck escaped, though not all of them were struck. They fled, rushing back along the road by which they had come.

text: Abraha was struck in his body, and they took him away with them.
say: Abraha was struck in his body, and they took him away with them.

text: Ibn Ishaq said: When Allah sent Muhammad ﷺ, among the blessings Allah reminded Quraysh of was His turning back the Abyssinians from them, for the sake of their survival. He, the Most High, said: [Surah al-Fil]
say: Ibn Ishaq said: When Allah sent Muhammad , peace be upon him,, among the blessings Allah reminded Quraysh of was His turning back the Abyssinians from them, for the sake of their survival. He, the Most High, said: [Surah al-Fil]

text: What Allah did to the People of the Elephant was not a victory for Quraysh … rather, the victory was for the Sacred House, as a sign and a preparation for the sending of Muhammad ﷺ.
say: What Allah did to the People of the Elephant was not a victory for Quraysh … rather, the victory was for the Sacred House, as a sign and a preparation for the sending of Muhammad , peace be upon him,.

text: I say: in its year the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was born, according to the well-known view.
say: I say: in its year the Messenger of Allah , peace be upon him, was born, according to the well-known view.

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib makes his camel rise…
say: Abdul Muttalib makes his camel rise…

text: What happened next was from Allah alone. No one could take part in it. Watch, and listen.
say: What happened next was from Allah alone. No one could take part in it. Watch, and listen.

text: You are an explorer in the valley of Makkah, in the days of ʿAbd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, when his son al-Harith was still his only son. Walk with W A S D or the arrow keys (or the pad on the screen), drag to look around, and go to the glowing lights.
say: You are an explorer in the valley of Makkah, in the days of Abdul Muttalib ibn Hashim, when his son al-Harith was still his only son. Walk with W A S D or the arrow keys (or the pad on the screen), drag to look around, and go to the glowing lights.

text: ʿAbd al-Muttalib slept here in al-Hijr, night after night. Listen to what he was told.
say: Abdul Muttalib slept here in al-Hijr, night after night. Listen to what he was told.

text: The description gave signs: the colony of the ants, and the crow with the white mark. Search the lights around the House for the place that shows both. (A game search: the other places are only for exploring.)
say: The description gave signs: the colony of the ants, and the crow with the white mark. Search the lights around the House for the place that shows both. (A game search: the other places are only for exploring.)

text: Only sand here.
say: Only sand here.

text: No sign of ants or a crow here.
say: No sign of ants or a crow here.

text: Ants are gathered here, and a crow with a white mark is pecking at the ground.
say: Ants are gathered here, and a crow with a white mark is pecking at the ground.

text: They had given up hope and sat waiting. What did ʿAbd al-Muttalib decide?
say: They had given up hope and sat waiting. What did Abdul Muttalib decide?

text: When all hope seemed gone, ʿAbd al-Muttalib chose to keep going and seek, and Allah gave them water. What can you keep going with, even when it feels hard?
say: When all hope seemed gone, Abdul Muttalib chose to keep going and seek, and Allah gave them water. What can you keep going with, even when it feels hard?

text: Far to the south, in Yemen, the ruler Abraha had a plan.
say: Far to the south, in Yemen, the ruler Abraha had a plan.

text: A messenger from the camp has come into Makkah, asking for the leader of Quraysh.
say: A messenger from the camp has come into Makkah, asking for the leader of Quraysh.

text: “I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.”
say: “I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord who will protect it.”

text: What did ʿAbd al-Muttalib mean?
say: What did Abdul Muttalib mean?

text: “The House has a Lord who will protect it.” ʿAbd al-Muttalib did his part, and trusted Allah with what was beyond him. When have you done your part and left the rest to Allah?
say: “The House has a Lord who will protect it.” Abdul Muttalib did his part, and trusted Allah with what was beyond him. When have you done your part and left the rest to Allah?
